name: BroadbandPicker
positioning: Independent UK broadband comparison. Compare deals by postcode, understand speeds and contracts, and switch without spending an evening on hold.
revenue_model: Free for consumers. Revenue from affiliate commissions when someone clicks through and signs up. Rankings are not sold. Providers can be listed with or without an affiliate relationship.

affiliate_and_ads.awin: Manual publisher review. Live, content-rich site beats a parked domain. Advertisers check promotional type, audience fit, brand-safety of neighbouring content, and whether similar ISPs already work with you. Social following is a supporting signal, not a substitute for the site. Comparison sites are an official Awin publisher type.
affiliate_and_ads.asa_cap: Affiliate links or codes in social copy make that post an ad. Label specific deal posts #ad / #affiliate, upfront. Organic jokes with no outbound deal link are brand content, but any hard claim ('cheapest in the UK', a named speed, a named price) still needs to be qualified and dated. Brand and affiliate are jointly on the hook.

curated.competitor_gap: Uswitch, MoneySuperMarket, Compare the Market, broadbandchoices and choose.co.uk talk like comparison engines. MoneySavingExpert talks like a consumer champion. Which? talks like a lab. None of them run a consistently funny, design-led UK broadband brand on TikTok. Instagram is the professional shopfront: providers judge the grid in three seconds. Which? has already called out ISPs for barely posting about social tariffs. X and TikTok take the sarcasm. Instagram takes the publisher look.

competitor_social.type: National comparison (RVU). Broadband + energy + mobiles. Awin/direct.
competitor_social.goal: Remain the default compare-and-switch brand; recruit Gen Z/millennials who do not open comparison sites.
competitor_social.social_move: Aug 2025: appointed Wilderness as social AOR. Brief is TikTok-first, Instagram/Facebook consultancy, 'major life stages' content. They are paying an agency because organic personality was missing.
competitor_social.what_they_post: Deal graphics, 'save £X', life-stage explainers once the agency lands. Historically TV + PPC, not a funny account.
competitor_social.handles_known: Site footer typically X/Facebook/YouTube. TikTok being built, not native-born.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: They will professionalise TikTok with an agency voice. They will not sound like a mate in a British kitchen. Occupy 'independent and actually funny about broadband' before their anniversary work fills the feed. Do not copy their save-£X red. Look more expensive than them, talk ruder.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Voucher red, 'save up to £395', meerkat energy, agency-smooth life-stage films.

competitor_social.type: National comparison + MSE + Quidco. Huge PPC. Affiliate + lead-gen.
competitor_social.goal: Defend against AI search eating comparison; SuperSaveClub loyalty; ChatGPT distribution.
competitor_social.social_move: 2025 marketing spend £194m. PPC costs +21%. They trialled moving mix out of PPC into social with 'initial good results', then still spent the money on brand + PPC. First UK comparison brand inside ChatGPT.
competitor_social.what_they_post: Brand films, club/loyalty, generic money-saving. Not broadband-native comedy.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: They buy attention. We cannot. We have to earn the first 1,000 followers with comments. Social is a side bet for them; it is the whole brand-build for us. They will never dunk on loyalty tax hard — they sell the same ISPs.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Superhero brand films, club points, 'we've helped UK families save £2.8bn'.

competitor_social.type: Consumer-champion publisher. Email list is the product. Affiliate on tools.
competitor_social.goal: Trust, email sign-ups, 'Martin said so'. Broadband is a tool, not a personality.
competitor_social.social_move: Facebook + Martin-as-news. Tips, warnings, TV clips. Almost no TikTok comedy.
competitor_social.what_they_post: Top deals, scam warnings, 'do this today'. Authority, not jokes.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: Do not compete on authority in week 1. Compete on shareability. When we do social tariffs, match their seriousness — that's the MSE lane we are allowed to borrow, because Which? already proved ISPs don't post it.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Martin-face thumbnails, 'THIS WEEKEND ONLY', email-capture everything.

competitor_social.type: Insurance-first comparison. Broadband is a tab. TV-ad brands.
competitor_social.goal: Brand recall (meerkat / Gio Compario), then quote. Social is TV residue.
competitor_social.social_move: YouTube ads, character IP, almost no broadband-native organic.
competitor_social.what_they_post: Characters, car insurance. Broadband is an afterthought.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: They own funny TV. They do not own funny broadband. Stay in our niche.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Mascots. Opera. Meerkats. BroadbandPicker is not a character.

competitor_social.type: Subscription consumer champion. Tests, not affiliate-first.
competitor_social.goal: Membership. Lab credibility. Policy noise (social tariffs).
competitor_social.social_move: X + Facebook as press office. Called out ISPs for not posting social tariffs.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: Borrow the social-tariff public-service post. Do not borrow the beige. Which? will never make a Keep Calm router poster.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Best Buy roundels, membership CTAs, lab-coat photography.

competitor_social.type: Broadband-specialist affiliate SEO sites. Our closest product comps.
competitor_social.goal: Postcode-checker sessions → Awin. Rank for 'cheap broadband'.
competitor_social.social_move: Thin or absent. SEO is the channel. Social is a neglected footer icon.
competitor_social.handles_known: Often a dormant Facebook or X.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: Specialist broadband affiliates in the UK almost do not do social. A designed, funny, independent specialist can look like the category leader in 30 days of posting — because nobody else is standing there.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: SEO-title posts ('Cheapest Broadband Deals UK 2026'), stacked logos, from-£19 banners.

competitor_social.goal: Clicks on merchant rates. Not a comparison publisher.
competitor_social.social_move: Facebook groups, 'hot rates', user community. High engagement, low prestige.
competitor_social.gap_for_us: Never look like a cashback account. Providers judge that in three seconds and reject Awin applications.
competitor_social.do_not_copy: Hot rate banners, emoji stacks, 'click our link'.

design_look: Match the BroadbandPicker poster system (the Engineer Window reference). 1) Full-bleed outer canvas in deep navy #0F172A. 2) A large rounded paper card #F8FAFC (corner radius 28-32px) sitting on the navy so a navy footer strip remains at the bottom. 3) Top of the card: one small sky-blue #0EA5E9 icon, centred (clock, wifi arc, kettle). 4) Headline in huge Inter ExtraBold navy #0F172A, 2 to 5 words, slightly tracked, British English. 5) A thin sky #0EA5E9 hairline under the headline. 6) One giant navy fact, time or price (example: 8AM-6PM). 7) A sky-blue sarcastic punchline under the fact, smaller than the headline (example: So... Tuesday.). 8) Illustration: clean editorial British cartoon, black/navy outlines, flat colour, limited palette navy/sky/grey/white. Split before/after or left/right panels with tiny navy time labels. Simple cartoon people (jumpers, slippers, glasses) not photoreal, not stock, not 3D, not celebrity. British terrace, kettle, mug, router, van, flask, pizza box, laptop allowed. 9) Navy footer: left-aligned sky rounded-square wifi-mark (two white arcs + white dot, like public/logo.svg) then white wordmark BroadbandPicker and URL broadbandpicker.co.uk in smaller white or sky type. 10) Matte. One joke. No extra slogans, no QR, no fake ISP logos, no SALE red, no emojis on the artwork, no 'comment below'.
